test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in Direct to Indirect Speech.

He said to me, "Where are you going?"

options.text: He asked me where I had gone.
He asked me where I am going.
He asked me where I go.
He asked me where I was going.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He asked me where I was going.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Question:** The direct question "Where are you going?" is converted into an indirect question "where I was going."
 
• **Verb tense:** The present continuous tense "are going" changes to the past continuous tense "was going" in indirect speech.
 
• **Pronoun:** The pronoun "you" changes to "I" to match the subject of the reporting verb.
 
• **Reporting verb:** The verb "said to" is replaced by "asked" to reflect the interrogative nature of the sentence.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• The direct speech question is not enclosed in quotation marks in indirect speech.
 
• The question mark is removed, as the indirect speech is a statement.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *He asked me where I was going.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "He asked me where I had gone."

 
 
• The past perfect tense "had gone" is incorrect as it changes the original meaning of the sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "He asked me where I am going."
 
 
• The present continuous tense "am going" is incorrect in indirect speech, as the reporting verb "said" requires a past tense conversion.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "He asked me where I go."
 
 
• The simple present tense "go" is incorrect, as it does not match the original continuous action in the direct speech.
